h: Conservation Roots and West Cornwall Days Out
p: Paradise Park has a proper conservation pedigree. It's the birthplace of the World Parrot Trust, the international charity founded here by the park's owner Mike Reynolds in 1989, which now works to protect wild parrots around the globe. The park has also been closely involved with efforts to bring back the Cornish chough, the red-billed crow that features on Cornwall's coat of arms and returned to breed on the county's cliffs in the early 2000s after decades away. Knowing that gives your visit a lovely bit of extra meaning.

Allow a good few hours, especially if the kids are going to want some time in JungleBarn, and check what talks and displays are on as you arrive. Feeding sessions and bird displays are where you'll learn the most and see the animals at their liveliest. Hayle is just off the A30, which makes it simple to reach from right across west Cornwall.

The surrounding area is packed with options. Godrevy, at the far end of the towans, has a lighthouse on an island offshore that inspired Virginia Woolf, and seals often haul out in the coves along the headland, best viewed from the clifftop paths. St Michael's Mount, the tidal island with a castle on top in Mount's Bay, is a short drive south, and you can walk across the causeway at low tide or take a little boat when the water is in. St Ives, with its harbour, beaches and Tate gallery, is a trip in itself, and the branch line railway along the coast from St Erth gives some of the loveliest views in Cornwall.
